title: CASE OF HYDE PARK AND OTHERS v. MOLDOVA (Nos. 5 and 6)
conclusion: Preliminary objections dismissed (victim, non-exhaustion of domestic remedies);Remainder inadmissible;Violation of Art. 11;Pecuniary and non-pecuniary damage - awards
summary: In the case of Hyde Park and Others v. Moldova, the applicants were members of Hyde Park, a non-governmental organisation known for advocating freedom of expression and assembly, which included individuals identifying as part of the Roma and Traveller communities. The case concerned the Moldovan authorities’ interference with their right to peaceful protest. Between August and September 2007 in Chişinău, Hyde Park organised several demonstrations against alleged harassment by state bodies. Despite initial authorisation for a protest on 30 August 2007, the Municipal Council’s permission was challenged by the Prosecutor General’s Office, leading to the applicants’ arrests and the premature end of the protest. Subsequent protests on 4 and 10 September were met with arrests and fines, often justified by procedural grounds such as late applications or incomplete authorisation details. The applicants also faced police searches and detention without access to legal counsel. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Article 11, which protects freedom of assembly and association. It found violations of this right, noting that the authorities’ actions were disproportionate and unjustified. The Court awarded pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages to the applicants. This judgment is significant as it reaffirms the protection of peaceful assembly rights for Roma and Traveller activists in Eastern Europe, a region where such minorities have historically faced systemic discrimination and state repression.
